PRIORITY: Technical scoping notes for matrix (draft)

Hi team —

I reviewed their dataflow and sketched a short matrix. High-level technical answers below (we'll formalize into a one-page matrix for legal):

1) Input persistence: Hosted API 
   - Request bodies (inputs) are processed in-memory by the serving runtime. By default we retain request logs and request/response metadata for 30 days for debugging/abuse detection; raw request bodies are not stored long-term unless debugging is enabled or customer opts into longer retention.
   - We can offer a Hosted configuration with reduced telemetry (no request body retention) and a 7-day max retention window for request metadata.

2) KV/Prefix caching: 
   - Prefix / KV caching is used to reduce repeated context cost. By default caches are ephemeral and tied to model server lifecycle; customers on Hosted do not get persistent tenant-shared caches that contain raw PHI across sessions. However, short-lived KV entries may exist in memory during active sessions.

3) Logs & analytics: 
   - Aggregated metrics (latency, token counts) do not contain PHI. Error traces may include sanitized fragments; we have a policy to redact long strings resembling SSNs or MRNs, but it's not a formal PHI scrub.

4) Dedicated / Private options: 
   - Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools for the customer; we can configure zero retention for request bodies and disable telemetry forwarding to multi-tenant analytics. Logs/audit trails remain available to the customer and to Redwood per SLA.
   - Private (VPC / on-prem): Full customer-controlled network and storage; Redwood's control plane can be configured to not ingest any request bodies. This is the recommended path if Sentry requires zero Redwood access to PHI.

5) Encryption and key management: 
   - All data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest is AES-256. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) so Redwood cannot decrypt stored artifacts without customer consent.

Attachments I plan to include with the matrix: hosted_retention_matrix.csv (shows default vs reduced vs dedicated/private), and an excerpt of our BAA clause that explicitly calls out retention windows and telemetry controls.

I'll prepare the one-page matrix and a recommended deployment for the patient-upload pipeline (short-term: Hosted with reduced telemetry for a PoC; production: Dedicated or Private depending on legal appetite).

Laura Bennett

Sara —

Thanks for the fast follow-ups. Quick summary + next steps: 

1) Suggested retained wording for Contracts (Hosted Reduced Telemetry):
   "Redwood will not retain raw request bodies containing protected health information (PHI) for more than 7 calendar days when the Hosted Reduced Telemetry configuration is enabled. Aggregated metrics and anonymized traces may be retained for the purposes of service reliability and abuse detection, but Redwood will not persist customer-provided PHI in long-term storage under this configuration."

2) Error traces: 
   - We do not intentionally persist full provider note text in error traces. That said, error traces may contain short, unsanitized snippets for debugging. For Sentry's production pipeline we recommend Dedicated or Private if you require zero possibility of snippet retention.

3) Deliverables attached to this thread for your review: hosted_retention_matrix.csv, one-page-scope-matrix.pdf (I uploaded the matrix to our Confluence and attached a PDF excerpt).

4) BAA / timeline: Mina will confirm contract language tweaks. We can provide a DocuSign-ready BAA template and a redlined clause that matches the 7-day Hosted Reduced Telemetry option.

Next: I'll set up a 30-min call for Monday to walk the matrix + deployment recommendation. If you want the BAA earlier, let me know and we can push the template to Contracts today.

Cheers,
